meta.title: Referral to First Treatment: What Changed and What Is Next
meta.subtitle: Half the Drop-off, Same Team, Two Asks
meta.decision: Adopt the three intake changes in every region by Jan 15
meta.big_idea: Three small intake changes halved the referrals we lose before first treatment, and every region can adopt them by January.
meta.notes: Synthetic example data for the skill self-test. Not real results.

slides.title: Three Intake Changes Halved Referral Drop-off
points: We now lose 1 in 10 referrals, down from 1 in 5
The fixes cost no new headcount
Every region can adopt them by Jan 15
slides.notes: Lead with the answer, then show where referrals were lost and what fixed it.

slides.title: One Quarter Later, We Lose Half as Many Referrals
points: Biggest gain came at the first call
Results held in every pilot clinic
slides.notes: The headline result: drop-off fell by almost half in one quarter without adding people.

slides.title: Most Referrals Were Lost Before Anyone Called
slides.takeaway: Calling within one day is where a single fix recovers the most patients.
slides.alt: Funnel from 1,200 referrals received to 610 first treatments, with the contact stage highlighted.
slides.notes: The largest loss was between receiving a referral and reaching the patient. That is where we focused first.

slides.title: Three Changes Closed the Biggest Gaps

cards.label: Call Within One Day
cards.detail: Schedulers make the first call by the next business day

cards.label: One Owner per Referral
cards.detail: A named scheduler follows it to the first visit

cards.label: Text Before Calling
cards.detail: Patients know who will call and why

slides.notes: The first change drove most of the gain; the other two kept patients from dropping later.

slides.title: More Patients Reached Their First Treatment
slides.label: Patients per Quarter
slides.text: Across the pilot clinics, at the same staffing level.
slides.notes: Pause here: this is the patient impact, not just a process metric.

slides.title: Every Pilot Region Improved, and West Improved Most
slides.takeaway: West started first, so the gain grows with time on the new process.
slides.alt: Column chart of drop-off reduction by region, West highest at 56 percent.
slides.notes: All four regions improved by at least 41 percent. West had the longest run time.

slides.text: The fixes are habits, not headcount.
slides.notes: Breather before the rollout detail: this is why every region can adopt them quickly.
